A few months ago, if someone had asked me what I wanted to do with my life, I probably would’ve answered with a job title. Today, I think I'd answer differently. I recently had the chance to sit down with Farah Bernier, ICF ACC, ELI-MP on her podcast, Living Fabulously Fierce, and somewhere in our conversation, she asked me why I call myself a "sillyologist" on my social media bio. I laughed. Then I realized being a sillyologist has very little to do with being silly. It's about perspective. I shared a story about losing all of my swimming gear at a gym. I could've been frustrated. Instead, I joked that whoever took it must have had great taste, and I hoped they enjoyed wearing it. Thirty seconds later, I had already moved on. I then talked about a moment from solo traveling to Botswana on New Year’s Eve. I asked my safari guide what his New Year's resolution was. He shook his head and said, “I’ve done so much this year. A lot of them weren’t in my plans. Things will come to you.” That was when I realized that maybe the greatest resolution isn’t another milestone to chase. Maybe it's staying open to whatever life has waiting around the next corner. The past few years have challenged so many of my assumptions about success, work, and happiness. Leaving consulting earlier this year wasn't about running away from something. It was about moving toward a life where my work and my joy no longer felt like separate things. I'm still figuring it all out. But if there's one thing I've learned, it's that the stories we tell ourselves about our circumstances often matter more than the circumstances themselves. Grateful to Farah for creating a space for conversations like this. If you're navigating change, redefining success, or simply trying to see life through a different lens, I hope something in our conversation resonates with you. Listen to the full conversation🎙️: Spotify - https://lnkd.in/gJSM-uR9 Apple Podcast - https://lnkd.in/gzrfbfW5 Watch my “silly” content here ☁️: https://lnkd.in/gN7_82Rc #Storytelling #PersonalGrowth #CareerTransition #Perspective #CreatorEconomy

Today, we're announcing Simile 's Series B. We've raised over $200M at a $2B post-money valuation, co-led by Greenoaks and Index Ventures with participation from Hanabi Capital , A*, Bain Capital Ventures (BCV) , CVS Health Ventures , and Definition . Our mission is to simulate all eight billion people on Earth, accurately. We’re building a future where every important decision is tested by simulating how people think, decide, and behave before ideas meet the real world. Leading organizations including CVS Health, Wealthfront, Deloitte, and Gallup use Simile to test business-critical decisions before they reach the real world – from validating customer research and shaping product strategy to designing customer experiences, communications, and policy before deployment. In just five months since launch, we've grown revenue 5x, built a new foundation model for human behavior, run tens of millions of simulations for Fortune 100 organizations, and grown from a small team in Palo Alto to more than 50 people worldwide. We're hiring researchers, engineers, designers, and operators to help build what's next: https://lnkd.in/guasYq8J . Thank you to our customers, investors, partners, and team for believing in our vision.

Some recent news: after an incredible run at Amazon/Amazon Games, I've started a new chapter as a Software Engineer at Adyen! 🎉 My time at Amazon was everything I could have asked for. I learned an enormous amount and had a great time working on some really cool tech. Amazon was my first job out of college and it really became a large part of my life over the last ~6 years. What I'll miss most though, is the people. I was lucky to work alongside truly incredible teammates and a top-notch manager who pushed me to grow while always having my back. My team was undoubtedly the best there was at Amazon, and I was so lucky to get to work with all of them. Beyond my immediate team, I met so many great people across the company, both through work directly and through the Arabs@Amazon ERG, which gave me connections and friendships I'll carry with me for a long time. The ERG did a lot for bringing a voice to Arabs and specifically Palestinians throughout the genocide, and I really appreciated the work they did and continue to do. Thank you to everyone who made my Amazon journey what it was! I hope to stay in touch, do not be a stranger! To my new colleagues at Adyen, I’m excited to dive in and start building! I am grateful to have already connected with so many of you in Amsterdam at our company offsite. I look forward to working with you all in such a dynamic fintech industry!

Almost ten years ago, I was introduced to the founders of Lime. At the time, they had little more than a deck and a bold vision for micromobility. One line from that deck has stayed with me ever since: “We want to reinvent urban mobility in America by learning from China” It was a contrarian idea. While many saw the rise of China’s internet ecosystem through the lens of competition, Lime’s founders saw an opportunity to learn. They believed great ideas can come from anywhere. I had no choice but to support their mission. Today, Lime is a public company. The journey was far from smooth, but that willingness to learn where others dismissed, and to find synergy where others saw rivalry, proved to be a strength. The lesson feels even more relevant today. Contrarian thinking is not about being different for the sake of being different. It is about staying open-minded enough to learn from unexpected places—and recognizing opportunity where others see only competition. Thank you Brad Bao and Toby Sun for starting the company! Congratulations Wayne Ting and team on this major milestone for Lime!
